newsitem.title: USA: Aluminum use in Europe cars seen doubling by 2005.
newsitem.headline: Aluminum use in Europe cars seen doubling by 2005.

text.p: Use of aluminum in European cars is forecast to more than double by the year 2005 to 130 to 150 kg per car, from 65 kg this year, pushing overall aluminum demand in the sector to two million tonnes, Dick Dermer, secretary general of the European Aluminum Association, said.
"Aluminum is well suited for both low and high volume production," Dermer said in remarks prepared for delivery at an industry conference.
Some European cars already use the higher amounts of aluminum, such as the Renault Safrane with 136 kg and the Volvo 960 with 140 kg, Dermer said.
Others such as the BMW Series 5, the Volkswagen Polo and Seat were looking to use more aluminum.
In 1994 car manufacturing accounted for 18 percent of Europe's aluminum demand, amounting to 65,000 tonnes in extruded and rolled products and one million tonnes in castings.
As cars use more aluminum, much of the extra metal will be in the form of extruded and rolled products rather than castings, Dermer said.
Some 95 percent of cars in Europe are recycled, and 95 percent of aluminum in each car is recycled.

"The overall secondary aluminium market in Europe amounted to 1.71 million tonnes in 1995, which was 4.57 percent higher than the year before," Dermer said. "It is expected that in 1996 these figures will change little."
